newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada has "no interest at all" in wheat cap to US.
newsitem.headline: Canada has "no interest at all" in wheat cap to US.

text.p: Canada has "no interest at all" in limiting wheat exports to the United States in the current crop year, Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale's spokesman said.

"There is no interest at all in a cap. Canada is trading fairly and freely with the United States under all existing trading rules. The level of exports to the U.S. are up from last year but nowhere near the level of 1993/94. Under the new trade agreements there are no caps," Goodale spokesman Vern Greenshields told Reuters in an interview.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture head of Foreign Agriculture Service told a U.S. House Agriculture subcommittee earlier Thursday that Canada had said it "would try not to exceed" 1.4 to 1.5 million tonnes of wheat and barley exports to the U.S.
Canada agreed in 1994 to cap wheat and durum wheat exports to the U.S. at 1.5 million tonnes after it exported more than that amount in the 1993/94 (Aug/July) crop year to the U.S.
Extensive flooding of the Mississippi River that year cut U.S. output and led to the higher-than-usual Canadian shipments.
But the deal struck in 1994 ended Sept 12, 1995, in accordance with new World Trade Organization and North American Free Trade Agreement rules.
North Dakota farmers in recent weeks asked U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshevsky to reinstate the cap.

"I know Ms. Barshevsky was listening to farmers in the northern states. I don't recall her saying anything in terms of commitments outside of the fact that she was willing to listen and they (U.S. government) have been talking about having meetings with us," Greenshields said.
